title: Opportunistic kernel bundling + pinned-host pool to cut small-batch overheads
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background:
Running production inference workloads reveals a persistent host-side cost pattern: large numbers of small prefill/decode microbatches cause repeated host->device pin/unpin operations, a high count of short DMA transfers, and scatter across threadpool workers which increases cache churn and cross-core contention. This disproportionately hurts low-latency small-request workloads and increases per-token CPU spend.

Goal:
Introduce an event-driven opportunistic bundling layer in the runtime scheduler that (1) groups compatible small prefill/decode work into short, latency-bound bundles for a single kernel dispatch, (2) reuses a compact pinned-host-memory pool to avoid repeated pin/unpin thrash, and (3) enforces cooperative worker backpressure/affinity to reduce threadpool contention. Additionally, add kernel selection hints so the bundler picks fused attention kernels for contiguous bundles and falls back to split kernels for high-variance sequence-length mixes.

Non-goals:
This ticket does not change model semantics, transformer math, or add new quantization paths. It focuses on host-side orchestration, memory management, and scheduling.

Design summary:
- Event-driven bundler: each incoming prefill/decode request is assigned a short slack window (configurable, default 0.8 ms). If other compatible requests (same model variant, compatible sequence-length bucket, same GPU affinity and quantization profile) arrive within the window, they are batched into a bundle and dispatched as a single kernel invocation.
- Compatibility rules: strict match on model binary + quantization profile, and sequence length within a tight bucket (e.g., +/ - 8 tokens) to preserve kernel efficacy.
- Bundling limits: bundle size capped by per-GPU throughput budget and latency SLOs; per-bundle max tokens and max wall time.
- Pinned-host pool: maintain an LRU pool of pre-pinned host buffers segmented by buffer size class. Give preference to reusing existing pinned buffers before allocating/pinning new ones. Pool size is tunable and auto-evicts under memory pressure.
- Cooperative worker backpressure: replace blind threadpool hand-offs with token-bucket-based admission and per-core dispatch hints so the same worker handles the entire bundle lifecycle (serialize enqueue->memcpy->dispatch->postprocess) where possible. This reduces cross-core cache misses and expensive parking/unparking.
- Kernel-selection hints: bundler queries the kernel-selector with bundle statistics (aggregate seq_len distribution, total token count) to prefer fused attention kernels for contiguous dense bundles, and to choose tiled/split kernels for bundles with high variance.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype a lightweight bundler in the runtime scheduler as an opt-in flag. Start with a single GPU-target path to simplify affinity concerns.
2) Implement pinned-host pool in the host-side allocator; expose pool size and eviction policy parameters via runtime config.
3) Add token-bucket admission to existing threadpool + per-worker affinity hinting.
4) Wire bundler to kernel-selector and add simple heuristics for fused vs split attention.
5) Microbenchmark harness to generate small-batch traces (1-4 requests, 8-128 tokens) and full-scale workload traces for regression testing.
6) Iterate on slack window and bundle caps based on latency vs throughput Pareto frontier.
7) Canary rollout: enable for a small percentage of incoming traffic and monitor cost/latency regressions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Bundling could increase P99 latency for some request shapes. Mitigation: conservative default slack (0.8 ms) and per-route opt-out; SLO guardrails and auto-fallthrough to single-request dispatch when latency sensitivity detected.
- Risk: Pinned pool OOM on hosts with many tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant pool quotas and adaptive eviction; integrate with host memory pressure signals.
- Risk: Bundles mix incompatible sequence lengths and degrade kernel performance. Mitigation: strict compatibility buckets and kernel-selection feedback loop in experiments.

Success metrics (must be measured end-to-end):
- 95th-percentile prefill->dispatch latency reduction >= 20% on small-batch traces (1-4 request mixes).
- Host CPU user time per-token down >= 15% on synthetic and production-like traces.
- Number of pin/unpin operations per 1M requests reduced >= 60%.
- No statistically significant regression in output tokens or errors; all existing unit and integration tests pass.

Operational plan:
- Add observability: per-route "bundle_rate", "avg_bundle_size", "pin_pool_hit_rate", "memcpy_count_per_request", and kernel-selection events.
- Dashboard: new runtime-1.24 perf card with before/after and canary slices.
- Rollout stages: dev -> canary(5%) -> regional canary(25%) -> global. Abort conditions: P99 prefill latency increase > 10% for a route or error rates increase > 0.5%.

- Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/PR-### (WIP)

New observability metrics are emitted and visible in the runtime dashboard
Canary rollout completed with no SLO violations and automated rollback tests in place
All new unit/integration tests and benchmark harnesses committed
